title: When the White River Broke Its Century Mark
location: Noblesville corridor, White River, Indiana, USA
headline: Follow Noblesville corridor, White River, Indiana, USA across 4 real radar observations
introduction: From 11–17 August 2026 repeated thunderstorms dropped more than a foot of rain across parts of central Indiana. The White River set new records at Anderson and Noblesville, exceeding crests not seen since 1913, and Indianapolis declared a local disaster emergency. These four NISAR observations follow a focused corridor near Noblesville from late July through early September on one ascending track.
conclusion: The 16 August acquisition falls during the documented crest window; it measures radar response on a common grid and does not itself prove flood depth or mapped inundation extent. Later acquisitions provide follow-up views only. Vegetation, wet soil, urban surfaces and geometry also change brightness. This story does not estimate flooded area, damage or evacuation needs.

method: NISAR, consistent polarization and orbit per story. Source calibrated power converted using 10*log10 where necessary; existing dB sources are not converted again. Bilinear alignment to the first grid, invalid/nonpositive power masked, fixed viridis −30 to +5 dB display. Statistics are radar response, not classified flood area.
eventEvidence: Documented by NWS Indianapolis and contemporaneous Indiana reporting; radar observations are not a validated flood classification.
